title: TTL: Add support for TTX Logger file format
description:
This MR adds support for the TTX Logger (TTL) file format by TTTech. It's the format the loggers from that company produce and is used in the automotive industry.

I decided to open the MR while my work is still ongoing in order to accept suggestions and comments.

## What is done
- [x] Ethernet/CAN/LIN/FlexRay support
- [x] Support for segmented entries
- [x] Interface names
- [x] Information extraction from configuration XML
- [x] Read master address and interface name from preference files

## What's missing (can be done with future MRs)
- [ ] Complete file dissector
- [ ] Ability to edit preference files from the UI

## Open points
- [ ] Split files
- [ ] Unsupported entries

### Split files
The format allows a capture file to be split in multiple parts, and a field in the header is the number of the split file.

Is there any way to handle this in Wireshark? I don't know if merging all the parts on the fly is the right approach, since logs can get very big.

Consider that any part is independent of each other and can be opened as-is.

### Unsupported entries
There are some entries that Wireshark doesn't currently support.

One of them is "Serial", that's just the capture of serial (UART) RX and TX data. Maybe we can use WTAP_ENCAP_WIRESHARK_UPPER_PDU. Or maybe there's already something better that I'm not aware of.

For other types, like MOST, there's an encapsulation type defined, but no dissector available.

Then there's the another type of entry: analog and digital signals. They represent physical and logical values, and a new packet is generated every time the value is sampled and/or updated.

### Other topics
- [ ] The code for `dissect_ttl_dest_addr_ret` and `dissect_ttl_src_addr_ret` is basically the same but I don't know how to make it generic.
- [ ] This MR depends on !18133

## Things to do before merging
- [ ] Extensive code review
- [x] Squash minor commits into main ones

### Example file
Unfortunately, I can't share any real file, but I created a file from scratch adding example entries in it.

[ttl_example_file.ttl](/uploads/34f4c768ade89ff998b87197ea687bef/ttl_example_file.ttl)

Is this file format documented anywhere?  If so, please cite it in a comment at the top of the file(s) (with URL, if the documentation is available online).

This is a little bit tricky. The documentation is available on the company's website, but only after you've registered, been approved and given access to the specific resource. So, even if the title page of the PDF says "Security: Public", I don't think I can re-upload it.

> The documentation is available on the company's website

So put in the URL and let the user go through the effort of getting approval if they want to read it.

This should probably eventually be reported to the user, either as a `WTAP_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` or, if we modify libwiretap to allow warnings to be reported, as a warning that includes the encapsulation value.

Returning false with an error will stop the processing of the file. That's why besides the return value, there's the supported parameter. During liner read, a return value of true, but supported put to false will simply skip the entry, while during the random read it will be treated as an error (meaning we did something wrong during the first pass).

This in itself is not an error, it's just that the entry represents other stuff we can't handle in Wireshark (yet).

> This in itself is not an error, it's just that the entry represents other stuff we can't handle in Wireshark (yet).

That's why I said "or, if we modify libwiretap to allow warnings to be reported, as a warning that includes the encapsulation value". We need to let the user know directly via the UI; unfortunately, we can't currently do that conveniently - I guess we could pop up a dialog from wiretap/ttf.c, but if there's a lot of that, dismissing the dialogs will get tiresome, so what we'd want would be something that shows up in the packet list and details in Wireshark and in TShark when printing dissection information, and in warning messages in command-line programs that aren't showing dissection information.

For now, we may be stuck with what we're doing now, but we should probably put in an XXX comment noting that we should do something better when we can.
Please take a look at the latest change. The return types should me more clear, and I added a comment as you suggested.

I see that not all file extensions are mentioned in that file. Why is that? I also see that in wiretap/file_access.c other files are mentioned, for macOS, freedesktop.org and Windows. Where exactly should I add it?

> I see that not all file extensions are mentioned in that file. Why is that?

File extensions for file formats that aren't capture files, but that our quasi-Fileshark capabilities can dissect; that's what the comment

```
; ============================================================================
; Push our known file extensions onto the stack, prepended with a marker
; Note that this is a subset of all the extensions for files that
; Wireshark can read. We probably don't want to grab JPEG or MP3 files.
; ============================================================================
```

is referring to.  If there are any *capture file* extensions missing, what are they?  Perhaps they're missing unintentionally.

> I also see that in wiretap/file_access.c other files are mentioned, for macOS, freedesktop.org and Windows. Where exactly should I add it?

All of those files.
